families.company: GE HealthCare (GE Medical Systems Ultrasound and Primary Care Diagnostics, LLC; manufacturer GE Vingmed Ultrasound AS)
deployment: vendor-neutral (DICOM from non-GE systems; raw-data from GE Vivid)
on-premise (centralized DICOM server deployment; remote access via Citrix per company page)
families.summary: EchoPAC is GE HealthCare's offline review, quantification and reporting workstation software for Vivid raw data and DICOM ultrasound images, offered as standalone software or as a PACS plug-in. K200852 carried the AI Auto Measure 2D and AI Auto Measure Spectrum Recognition features (cleared on Vivid E95 K200743) plus AFI 3.0/Auto EF 3.0/AFI RV/AFI LA into EchoPAC; K220940 added the AI Auto ROI-based Easy AutoEF and Easy AFI LV; K251342 added the AI Cardiac Auto Doppler spectral-tracing algorithms and 4D valve/chamber tools. K220940 reports Dice accuracy for the Auto ROI algorithm; K251342 reports Doppler test-set sizes and BMI-subgroup agreement; K200852 reports no performance data. None of the three clearances required a clinical study.
families.intended_use_quote: EchoPAC Software Only / EchoPAC Plug-in is intended for diagnostic review and analysis of ultrasound images, patient record management and reporting, for use by, or on the order of a licensed physician.
families.indications_for_use_quote: EchoPAC Software Only / EchoPAC Plug-in is intended for diagnostic review and analysis of ultrasound images, patient record management and reporting, for use by, or on the order of a licensed physician. EchoPAC Software Only / EchoPAC Plug-in allows post-processing of raw data images from GE ultrasound scanners and DICOM ultrasound images. Ultrasound images are acquired via B (2D), M, Color M modes, Color, Power, Pulsed and CW Doppler modes, Coded Pulse, Harmonic, 3D, and Real time (RT) 3D Mode (4D). Clinical applications include: Fetal/Obstetrics; Abdominal (including renal and GYN); Urology (including prostate); Pediatric; Small organs (breast, testes, thyroid); Neonatal and Adult Cephalic; Cardiac (adult and pediatric); Peripheral Vascular; Transesophageal (TEE); Musculo-skeletal Conventional; Musculo-skeletal Superficial; Transrectal (TR); Transvaginal (TV); Intraoperative (vascular); Intra-Cardiac; Thoracic/Pleural and Intra- Luminal.

Easy AFI LV (AFI 3.0 with AI Auto ROI algorithm) - K220940

clearances.changes_summary: Primary predicate EchoPAC Software Only / EchoPAC Plug-in (K170847); reference predicates Vivid S70N (K182450), Vivid E95 (K181685), Vivid E95 (K200743). Feature additions (all 'same feature as cleared on Vivid E95 K200743'): AI Auto Measure - 2D (semi-automated PLAX measurements), AI Auto Measure - Spectrum Recognition (automated recognition of Doppler spectra starting Auto Doppler), AFI 3.0 and Auto EF 3.0 (based on AFI 2.0/Auto EF 2.0 of K181685; extended to third-party DICOM images), AFI RV, AFI LA, Launchpad, FlexiLight and HD Color, 4D Auto TVQ (based on 4D Auto MVQ of K170847), DICOM PDF Read, Open 4D (third-party 3D/4D import), Z-score enhancement, 4D marker enhancement. Indications: added Obstetrics, Intra-luminal and Intra-Cardiac (cleared with Vivid S70N K182450); clarified Real time 3D as 4D. No performance data reported; no clinical studies required. Summary dated March 27, 2020.

training_data.description: K251342 (AI Cardiac Auto Doppler): Tissue Doppler development dataset 1482 recordings from 4 unique clinical sites; Doppler Trace development dataset 2070 recordings from 4 unique clinical sites (sites not used for testing); development images from M5Sc, M5S, 4Vc, 4V, M4S, 6S, 12S, 6Vc, 6VT probes on Vivid E80, E95, E9, 7, S70N. Patient counts for development sets not stated. K220940 (Auto ROI): training set size not stated; only that training and test sites differ.

validation_data.description: K251342: Tissue Doppler test set 4106 recordings / 805 individuals; Doppler Trace test set 3390 recordings / 1369 individuals; 9 countries; 8 Vivid consoles; 14 probe entries listed (M5S appears twice, i.e. 13 unique); adult and pediatric; BMI subset 41 patients / 433 measurements. K220940: 135 images from 45 exams (Europe, Asia, US; 5 probes, 4 consoles).

prior_validations.description: Company page (fetched this session) states: results 'in 1-click and less than 15 seconds with Easy AutoEF and Easy AFI LV'; 'AI Auto Measure Spectrum Recognition and AI Auto Measure 2D'; multi-vendor 2D and 4D DICOM; 'centralized DICOM server deployment'; 'Remote access is enabled by Citrix'. Company claims; no supporting data on the page.
Peer-reviewed comparisons of the earlier GE AutoEF and 4D Auto LVQ tools against Simpson biplane and CMR (Aurich 2014, n=47; Myhr 2018, n=100) predate the AI Auto ROI versions cleared in K220940.

papers.title: Assessment of left ventricular volumes with echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging: real-life evaluation of standard versus new semiautomatic methods
papers.key_result: 47 patients: GE Auto-EF vs Simpson r=0.85, bias 3%, LOA 12%; 4D Auto LVQ (3DE) vs Simpson r=0.79, bias 3%, LOA 14%; vs CMR Auto-EF r=0.74, bias 9%, LOA 17% and 3DE r=0.73, bias 9%, LOA 17%; intra/interobserver variability 6%/12% (Auto-EF) and 8%/11% (3DE); significant underestimation of volumes and EF vs CMR. (Pre-AI-Auto-ROI versions of the tools; abstract names the GE tool names, not EchoPAC.)

papers.title: Semi-automated estimation of left ventricular ejection fraction by two-dimensional and three-dimensional echocardiography is feasible, time-efficient, and reproducible
papers.key_result: Feasibility AutoEF 86%, 4D Auto LVQ 89%; 4D Auto LVQ underestimated LVEF vs Simpson biplane by -2 +/- 8%; AutoEF and 4D Auto LVQ had lowest test-retest variability (intra-examiner CV 10-11%, inter-examiner CV 10-12%). (Pre-AI-Auto-ROI versions.)

papers.title: Automated Measurements of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction During Cardiac Surgery by Transesophageal Echocardiography: Auto-EF Study.
papers.key_result: 180 adult cardiac-surgery patients, 4 hospitals (India), retrospective TEE: Auto-EF in EchoPAC v206 vs manual biplane method of disks; ICC for EF 0.84 (95% CI 0.68-0.91); r 0.95 EDV, 0.94 ESV, 0.88 EF; mean difference 3.30%, LOA -8.03 to 14.64%; kappa for EF grade 0.72; 72.2% correctly classified. (Whether v206 Auto-EF is the AI Auto ROI version of K220940 is not stated.)

papers.title: Reliability and feasibility of automated function imaging for quantification in patients with left ventricular dilation: comparison with cardiac magnetic resonance.
papers.key_result: 50 patients with LV dilation: GE AFI (auto and semi-auto) vs CMR; EF correlation r=0.81 (auto-AFI) and 0.86 (semi-auto-AFI); AFI underestimated LV volumes vs CMR (P<0.01) but not vs Simpson biplane. (Abstract names AFI, GE Healthcare; platform - scanner vs EchoPAC - not stated.)

papers.title: Intervendor agreement for left atrial strain via speckle tracking echocardiography in pediatrics.
papers.key_result: 89 children (30 HCM, 59 normal): GE EchoPAC AFI LA vs TomTec AutoStrain LA; ICCs 0.85-0.92 (GE vs TomTec at acquired frame rate); GE absolute LAS lower by 3.99% (bias) vs TomTec.

papers.title: Vendor and software based variation in left atrial strain measurements: implications for clinical practice.
papers.key_result: 112 subjects: GE AFI-LA vs GE EchoPAC LV-based strain (mid/endo) and TomTec-Arena feature tracking; r >= 0.7 for all; AFI-LA systematically underestimated LAS vs GE-endo and TomTec, smallest bias vs GE-mid; AFI-LA inter/intra-observer r > 0.85.

papers.title: Normal ranges of right atrial strain by contemporary echocardiography software: a prospective comparative cohort study.
papers.key_result: 100 healthy subjects (50% GE, 50% Philips scans): RA strain by TomTec 51.02 (AutoStrain LA), EchoPAC 206 (AFI-LA), VVI, Epsilon; RASr mean (LLN) 41.2% (29.6) TomTec vs 35.9% (27.0) EchoPAC; EchoPAC worked only on GE scans.

papers.title: Reference Ranges of Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain by Contemporary Vendor-Neutral Echocardiography Software in Healthy Subjects.
papers.key_result: 100 healthy subjects: LVGLS mean (LLN) -17.1% (-14.7%) TomTec 51.02 AutoStrain LV vs -17.8% (-14.4%) EchoPAC 206 AFI-LV; EchoPAC vs TomTec beta -0.62 (-1.2, 0.0); feasible on both GE and Philips scans.

papers.title: Three-dimensional Versus Two-Dimensional Echocardiographic Assessment of Left Atrial Volume and Deformation in Children.
papers.key_result: 50 children: 3DE LA volume/strain by GE EchoPAC 4D Auto LAQ v206 (near fully automated) vs 2DE TomTec TTA2.51 CPA (manual); processing 0.6 vs 2.7 min; good agreement for LA volume, weak agreement for LA strain.

papers.title: Reliability of left ventricular global longitudinal strain across acquisition and analysis techniques: a prospective comparative study.
papers.journal: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract
papers.key_result: 254 patients: 2D GLS consistent between EchoPac and TomTec-Arena (ICC > 0.9 intra/interobserver); 3D GLS lower than 2D by 4.3% (mean difference).

papers.title: Impact of inter-vendor variability on evaluation of left ventricular mechanical dispersion.
papers.key_result: 59 subjects scanned on GE and Philips: LV mechanical dispersion by EchoPac, QLAB and TomTec Arena; bias between vendor-specific packages 17.6 ms (LOA -29.6 to 64.8, r 0.47); TomTec Arena across scanner vendors bias -3.1 ms (LOA -27.6 to 21.4, r 0.75).

papers.title: Inter-vendor comparison of left atrial strain using layer specific strain analysis.
papers.key_result: 128 individuals (88 no cardiac history, 40 PAF): GE EchoPAC mid-myocardial LAS systematically lower than TomTec-Arena v2.30.02 (reservoir MD -6.08%, LOA -12% to 0%); GE endocardial LAS no systematic bias (MD 0.41%, LOA -7% to 8%).

open_questions: K200852: the 510(k) summary body (FDA PDF pages 4-8) has no text layer (vector-outlined text); content was read from the rendered pages. It reports no performance data for any feature, including AI Auto Measure 2D and Spectrum Recognition.
K220940: training set size, number of training sites and patient demographics (sex, age) not stated; exact patient count in test set unknown due to anonymization (45 exams assumed 45 patients).

K251342: numeric mean-percent-absolute-error results and the feasibility score achieved are not reported (only that thresholds were passed); the BMI-subgroup 'predefined metric' is not defined in the summary; number of test sites not stated; patient counts for development datasets not stated.
K251342 lists the Vivid iq reference as both 'K2432260' (typo) and 'K243620'.

Whether the published NTNU/GE Vingmed deep-learning EF and GLS algorithms (Smistad 2020; Salte 2023; Holmstrøm 2025) are the algorithms deployed in Easy AutoEF / Easy AFI LV is not confirmed by any FDA or company source read.
No peer-reviewed validation of the AI Cardiac Auto Doppler feature was found in PubMed searches this session.
No clinicaltrials.gov record naming EchoPAC as the intervention was found; NCT07701369 uses an 'AutoEF-AI Assessment' arm but the device/vendor is not identified in the record.
Whether the Auto-EF in EchoPAC v206 evaluated by Borde 2026 and the AFI evaluated by Chen 2022 are the AI Auto ROI versions cleared in K220940 is not stated in those abstracts.

families.company: Philips Ultrasound, LLC (TOMTEC Imaging Systems GmbH platform)
families.summary: Ultrasound Workspace 6.0 is Philips' rebranded release of the TOMTEC-ARENA analysis platform (predicate K213544). K241659 added three machine-learning applications for adult cardiac use: Segmental Wall Motion scoring integrated into AutoStrain LV (2D Auto LV), 3D Auto TV tricuspid-annulus quantification, and 3D Auto CFQ mitral regurgitant volume and peak flow rate from 3D color Doppler, plus VeriSight ICE data compatibility. Bench validation compared SWM to DiA's LVivo SWM, 3D Auto TV to manual 4D Cardio-View, and 3D Auto CFQ to CMR regurgitant volume; no clinical investigation was performed.
families.intended_use_quote: Ultrasound Workspace is a clinical software package designed for review, quantification and reporting of structures and function based on multi-dimensional digital medical data acquired with different modalities.
families.indications_for_use_quote: Indications for use of the product are quantification and reporting of cardiovascular, fetal, and abdominal structures and function of patients with suspected disease to support the physician in the diagnosis.
embedded_ai_features: Segmental Wall Motion (SWM): machine-learning segmental wall motion scores for 17 LV segments and WMSI, integrated with AutoStrain LV as '2D Auto LV' (semi-automated; user-editable scores)
3D Auto TV: machine-learning model-based segmentation of the tricuspid annulus from 3D TEE/TTE with derived annulus measurements
3D Auto CFQ: semi-automated mitral regurgitation volume and peak flow rate from 3D color flow TEE using ML mitral-valve model plus fluid-dynamic flow model
3D Auto MV (predicate, formerly 4D MV-ASSESSMENT): ML landmark proposals for mitral valve model
AutoStrain LV/RV/LA and Auto Measure (predicate TOMTEC-ARENA features)

clearances.changes_summary: Introduces SWM (integrated into AutoStrain LV as 2D Auto LV), 3D Auto TV and 3D Auto CFQ applications and VeriSight ICE / Pro ICE data compatibility on UWS 6.0; general software architecture of TOMTEC-ARENA unchanged; indications unchanged; product code IYN newly added as secondary (with LLZ). Reference devices K240850 (EPIQ with SWM) and K202216 (EPIQ with ICE/Pro ICE).
notable_flags: QIH primary; LLZ and IYN secondary
semi-automated quantitative imaging per FDA TPA guidance
ground truth for SWM was another vendor's cleared algorithm (LVivo SWM, DiA Imaging Analysis)
CMR reference standard for 3D Auto CFQ

performance_claims.quote: The results showed a very strong correlation to the LVivo application for WMSI output (Pearsons's correlation coefficient of 0.957 (95%CI 0.933, 0.972 ), thereby meeting the predefined acceptance criteria for the study.

performance_claims.comparator: manual 4D Cardio-View measurements; inter-observer variability as reference

performance_claims.metric: mean relative error; limits of agreement
performance_claims.value: mean relative error within +/-1%; LoA within +/-5%

performance_claims.endpoint: 3D Auto CFQ mitral regurgitant volume agreement with CMR
performance_claims.value: LoA -49.29 to 25.09 mL; 95% CI lower LoA (-58.37, -40.20), upper LoA (16.01, 34.18); acceptance maximum allowable difference 61.6 mL
performance_claims.comparator: cardiac magnetic resonance regurgitant volume (ground truth)
performance_claims.dataset_description: TEE 3D color flow studies with paired CMR; sample size not stated
performance_claims.quote: This study produced limits of agreement (LoA) of -49.29 (lower LoA) and 25.09 (upper LoA) and associated confidence intervals: lower end of 95% LoA (-58.37,-40.20) and upper end of 95% LoA (16.01,34.18). The acceptance criteria set for the study was defined as maximum allowable difference (Δ) of 61.6 ml.

performance_claims.endpoint: 3D Auto CFQ regurgitant volume bias vs CMR
performance_claims.value: within +/-19.2 mL (acceptance criterion met; point estimate not reported)
performance_claims.quote: In addition, bias was assessed where the acceptance criteria for mean difference (bias) within +/ - 19.2ml was met.

performance_claims.endpoint: 3D Auto CFQ peak regurgitant flow rate vs 2D PISA
performance_claims.value: upper and lower 95% CI bounds >0.8 for both fully-automated and semi-automated modes (point estimate not reported)
performance_claims.comparator: 2D PISA method on the same subjects
performance_claims.quote: For both fully -automated and semi -automated 3D Auto CFQ, the upper and lower bounds of the 95% confidence interval for Pearson's correlation exceeded the acceptance criteria of > 0.8 when compared to 2D PISA.

training_data.description: K241659 does not state training set sizes for SWM, 3D Auto TV or 3D Auto CFQ. It states that 3D Auto TV uses the same contour-generation method as 3D Auto MV but 'trained on tricuspid valve images'. The predicate K213544 disclosed approx. 2,800 training studies for its semi-automated measurement CNN (see tomtec-arena family).

validation_data.description: Three retrospective bench studies (SWM vs LVivo SWM on TTE clips; 3D Auto TV on TEE/TTE clips read by 3 experts; 3D Auto CFQ on TEE vs CMR and 2D PISA) plus in-silico phantoms; sample sizes, sites and demographics not stated beyond 'broad range of demographics, body habitus' for 3D Auto TV.

prior_validations.description: Company page: Ultrasound Workspace 'built on the foundation of the TOMTEC-ARENA platform'; deployment 'single seat workstation to enterprise integration' with central hosting; analysis of multi-vendor data; Auto Measure, AutoStrain, 3D Auto MV/RV listed.

TOMTEC 3D Auto CFQ page: 'quantification of mitral valve regurgitant (MR) volume (RVol) and peak flow rate from a 3D Color Doppler acquisition'; part of Ultrasound Workspace; no numeric validation shown.
Kim et al. 2026 JASE: single-center retrospective TEE validation of 3D Auto CFQ in 185 MR patients with a 29-patient CMR subgroup (see papers).

papers.title: Mitral Regurgitation Assessment Using a Novel Automated Three-Dimensional Color-Flow Quantification: Comparison with Two-Dimensional Proximal Isovelocity Surface Area and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance
papers.key_result: 3D Auto CFQ feasibility 97.3%; intra/inter-observer ICC 0.96/0.91; RVol 36.3 +/- 25.2 mL vs 65.9 +/- 38.7 mL by 2D PISA (P<.001); fewer severe MR classifications (16.2% vs 53.3%); in 29-patient CMR subgroup, agreement with CMR r=0.860, ICC 0.92 vs 2D PISA r=0.694, ICC 0.64; weaker correlation in atrial fibrillation.

papers.title: Quantification of mitral regurgitation: from traditional methods to artificial intelligence
papers.key_result: Narrative review; PMC full text (PMC13267601) states '3D Auto Color Flow Quantification (3D Auto CFQ, Philips) ... has been validated against cardiac MRI' citing a 2024 Philips Ultrasound white paper; one author affiliated with Philips (Cambridge, USA). No new performance data.

open_questions: Sample sizes, number of sites, vendor mix and demographics for the SWM, 3D Auto TV and 3D Auto CFQ validation studies are not stated in K241659.
Training data sizes and sources for SWM, 3D Auto TV and 3D Auto CFQ are not disclosed; independence of test data from training data is not addressed in the summary.
SWM ground truth was another vendor's cleared algorithm (LVivo SWM, DiA), not expert wall-motion reads; no comparison to expert visual scoring is reported.
Point estimates of 3D Auto CFQ bias vs CMR and of Pearson r vs PISA are not given (only that acceptance criteria were met).
No peer-reviewed validation of 3D Auto TV or of the SWM feature as deployed in UWS was found in PubMed searches this session.
No clinicaltrials.gov record naming Ultrasound Workspace was found.
PubMed searches this session ('Ultrasound Workspace'; '3D Auto TV'/'3D Auto CFQ'/Philips segmental wall motion) returned no peer-reviewed validation of UWS 6.0 beyond Kim 2026 (3D Auto CFQ).

families.company: TOMTEC Imaging Systems GmbH (a Philips company)
deployment: zero-footprint web viewer (TOMTEC ZERO, added in TTA2.40)
families.summary: TOMTEC-ARENA is a vendor-independent echocardiography review, quantification and reporting platform with optional modules (IMAGE-COM, AutoStrain LV/RV/LA, 2D CPA, 4D LV-Analysis, 4D RV-Function, 4D MV-Assessment, 4D Cardio-View, Reporting). K201632 (TTA2.40) brought machine-learning contour generation from Philips QLAB HeartModel into 4D RV-Function and 4D MV-Assessment and packaged AutoStrain as a module; K213544 (TTA2.50) added a supervised CNN that proposes editable B-mode and Doppler caliper measurements, trained on approximately 2,800 studies and tested on approximately 500. Neither summary reports numeric accuracy results; the platform was later rebranded by Philips as Ultrasound Workspace (K241659).
families.intended_use_quote: TOMTEC-ARENA software is a clinical software package designed for review, quantification and reporting of structures and function based on multi-dimensional digital medical data acquired with different modalities.TOMTEC-ARENA is not intended to be used for reading of mammography images.
families.indications_for_use_quote: Indications for use of TOMTEC-ARENA software are quantification and reporting of cardiovascular, fetal, and abdominal structures and function of patients with suspected disease to support the physician in the diagnosis.
embedded_ai_features: Semi-automated B-mode and Doppler measurements via supervised-learning CNN (IMAGE-COM; caliper proposals editable by user) - K213544
4D RV-Function: 3D RV surface model created automatically by machine-learning algorithms (QLAB HeartModel segmentation engine integrated) - K201632
4D MV-Assessment: semi-automatic ML landmark proposals for mitral valve model - K201632
AutoStrain LV / RV / LA and AutoLV (automated contour detection and tracking for GLS and biplane EF) - K201632
4D LV-Analysis with LA option (3D speckle tracking)

clearances.changes_summary: TTA2.40: 4D RV-Function v3.0 integrates QLAB HeartModel ML auto-segmentation for RV border placement, adds EDVI/ESVI and .stl/.obj export; 4D MV-Assessment v2.5 adds ML-based semi-automatic landmark proposals and new MV measurements; 4D LV-Analysis v3.2 adds LA option (LA volumes, LA trueEF, LA GLS) and an ASE2015-adapted bullseye; AutoStrain bullseye changed from 16 to 18 segments; AutoStrain LV/LA/RV released as a dedicated module with LA strain parameters; IMAGE-COM v5.5 adds measurements, pediatric and cath exam types, and browser-based zero-footprint deployment (TOMTEC ZERO); Fetal 2D CPA; new Reporting workspaces. Primary predicate TomTec-Arena TTA2 (K150122); secondary predicate QLAB (K200974). Summary lists product code QIH; FDA letter and openFDA list LLZ.
notable_flags: product code discrepancy: letter LLZ vs summary QIH

clearances.changes_summary: TTA2.50: introduces semi-automated, editable echocardiographic measurements on B-mode and Doppler datasets using a supervised-learning convolutional neural network (approx. 2,800 training studies, approx. 500 test studies); no new measurement types; separately licensed; intended-use environment extended to inside and outside hospitals/clinics/offices; primary product code switched to QIH with LLZ secondary. Reference device Philips EPIQ/Affiniti with Auto Measure (K211597).
notable_flags: training and test set sizes disclosed

performance_claims.endpoint: AutoLV (TomTec-Arena 1.2) fully automated EF and longitudinal strain - feasibility and analysis time
performance_claims.value: feasible in 98% of studies; 8 +/- 1 s per patient
performance_claims.comparator: manual biplane Simpson tracing at local and reference centers
performance_claims.dataset_description: 255 patients in sinus rhythm from 4 centers (FAST-EFs); earlier TomTec-Arena 1.2 AutoLV, a predecessor of the AutoStrain/AutoLV modules in TTA2.40
performance_claims.quote: AutoLV measurements were feasible in 98% of studies, and the average analysis time was 8 ± 1 s/patient. Interclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis revealed good agreements among automated EF, local center manual tracking, and reference center manual tracking, but not for visual EF assessments.

performance_claims.endpoint: 3DE RV volumes and EF by 'new software' vs CMR (draft attributed to TomTec 4D RV-Function; the PubMed abstract names no vendor or product and the full text is paywalled)
performance_claims.value: EDV -15 +/- 24 mL; EF 1.4 +/- 4.9% with manual editing; fully automated option EF bias -17 +/- 10%
performance_claims.dataset_description: 47 prospectively studied patients (14-82 years, 28 men) with RV EDV 82-354 mL and EF 34-81% at CMR; attribution to the TomTec 4D RV-Function module is not confirmable from the abstract
performance_claims.quote: RV volumes and EF measurements by the new software had an excellent accuracy (bias ± SD: -15 ± 24 mL for EDV; 1.4 ± 4.9% for EF) and reproducibility compared with CMR, provided that the RV borders automatically tracked by software were systematically edited by operator. The automated analysis option underestimated the EDV, overestimated the ESV, and largely underestimated the EF (bias ± SD: -17 ± 10%).

performance_claims.endpoint: AutoLV EF and AutoSTRAIN GLS (TomTec) vs manual analysis in healthy children and young adults
performance_claims.comparator: manual analysis by an experienced sonographer
performance_claims.dataset_description: 50 normal volunteers (22 female / 28 male), prospective research echocardiography; fully automated analyses run by 5 observer groups
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Border detection achievable in all subjects; analysis time shorter than manual (p<0.001)
performance_claims.quote: Strong correlations were seen between conventional EF and AutoLV (r = 0.8373), and between conventional three view global longitudinal strain (GLS) and AutoSTRAIN (r = 0.9766).

training_data.description: K213544: 'The echocardiographic studies were randomly assigned to be either used for training (approx. 2,800 studies) or testing (approx. 500 studies).' Ground truth was measurements 'manually generated by qualified healthcare professionals'. Sites, vendors and demographics not stated. K201632 discloses no training data.

validation_data.description: K213544: approx. 500 studies set aside as a test pool at the beginning of the project; randomly assigned (same source pool as training). No accuracy results reported. K201632: software verification and summative usability only.

prior_validations.description: DAIC news (Aug 4, 2020): TomTec-Arena 2020 release announced AI measurement automation (mitral valve and endocardium detection, automated GLS and EF); 'pending commercial availability in United States' at that time; no performance numbers.
Philips Ultrasound Workspace page states the product is 'built on the foundation of the TOMTEC-ARENA platform'.
FAST-EFs multicenter study (Knackstedt 2015) validated the earlier TomTec-Arena 1.2 AutoLV fully automated EF and strain in 255 patients across 4 centers.

papers.title: Fully Automated Versus Standard Tracking of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction and Longitudinal Strain: The FAST-EFs Multicenter Study
papers.key_result: AutoLV (TomTec-Arena 1.2) feasible in 98%; 8 +/- 1 s per patient; good ICC/Bland-Altman agreement of automated EF with manual biplane Simpson at local and reference centers; automated EF and LS had zero variability.

papers.title: New speckle-tracking algorithm for right ventricular volume analysis from three-dimensional echocardiographic data sets: validation with cardiac magnetic resonance and comparison with the previous analysis tool
papers.key_result: 47 patients vs CMR: 'new software' EDV bias -15 +/- 24 mL, EF bias 1.4 +/- 4.9% with manual editing; fully automated option EF bias -17 +/- 10%; shorter analysis time (3-5 min) and lower inter-observer variability than previous software. The abstract does not name the vendor or software; attribution to TomTec 4D RV-Function is unconfirmed (full text paywalled).

papers.title: Measurement of Left Ventricular Dimensions and Ejection Fraction in Neonates by Three-Dimensional Echocardiography: A Comparative Study Between Philips QLAB and TOMTEC Software-Are the Values Interchangeable?
papers.key_result: 50 neonates recruited, 38 with full 3D datasets: LV dimensions, volumes and EF from the same 3DE datasets compared between Philips QLAB 9.0 and TomTec 4D LV-Analysis; PubMed abstract is truncated after the first result ('24.7 +/- 3.6 ml/m') so agreement statistics were not extracted.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Fully Automated Assessment of Left Ventricular Volume, Ejection Fraction and Strain: Experience in Pediatric and Young Adult Echocardiography.
papers.key_result: 50 normal volunteers: TomTec AutoLV EF vs conventional EF r=0.8373; AutoSTRAIN GLS vs three-view manual GLS r=0.9766; border detection achievable in all; analysis time shorter than manual; results consistent across 5 observer groups of differing expertise.

papers.title: Prediction of cardiac events using fully automated GLS and BNP titers in patients with known or suspected heart failure.
papers.key_result: 3,150 subjects: fully automated GLS (AutoStrain, TomTec) plus BNP; derivation (n=1,514) and validation (n=1,636) cohorts; GLS cut-offs 7% and 14% stratified cardiac death and MACE.

papers.title: Accuracy of fully automated right ventricular quantification software with 3D echocardiography: direct comparison with cardiac magnetic resonance and semi-automated quantification software.
papers.key_result: 100 patients with same-day CMR: fully automated Philips 3DE RV software vs semi-automated TomTec software vs CMR; RVEF by the semi-automated (TomTec) software was significantly larger than CMR (P<0.001); analysis time 120 s (TomTec) vs 15 s (fully automated). (TomTec module name not given in abstract.)

papers.title: Prognostic value of automated longitudinal strain measurements in asymptomatic aortic stenosis.
papers.key_result: 340 asymptomatic AS patients: fully automated LV/LA/RV LS by 'AutoStrain, Philips'; LVGLS independently associated with cardiac events (HR 0.873-0.888); 3-year event-free 89% vs 76% by median LVGLS 15.1%. (Abstract attributes AutoStrain to Philips; platform - TOMTEC-ARENA vs Philips on-cart - not stated.)

papers.title: Fully Automated Evaluation of Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain in Normal Hearts: An Assessment of Accuracy in the Pediatric Population.
papers.key_result: 168 pediatric patients: 'Philips AutoStrain' fully automated vs manual GLS R=0.71, semiautomated R=0.90; accuracy affected by image axis, age and apex visualization. (Abstract attributes AutoStrain to Philips; platform not stated.)

papers.title: Pediatric Normal Values and Z Score Equations for Left and Right Ventricular Strain by Two-Dimensional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiography Derived from a Large Cohort of Healthy Children.
papers.key_result: 1,032 healthy subjects <21 years (Philips EPIQ images): normal values and Z-score equations for TomTec AutoSTRAIN (LV and RV longitudinal strain) and QLAB 10.8; reliability greater for AutoSTRAIN than QLAB 10.8.

papers.title: Intervendor agreement for left atrial strain via speckle tracking echocardiography in pediatrics.
papers.key_result: 89 children (30 HCM, 59 normal): GE EchoPAC AFI LA vs TomTec AutoStrain LA; ICCs 0.85-0.92 (GE vs TomTec at acquired frame rate); GE absolute LAS lower by 3.99% (bias) vs TomTec.

papers.title: Vendor and software based variation in left atrial strain measurements: implications for clinical practice.
papers.key_result: 112 subjects: GE AFI-LA vs GE EchoPAC LV-based strain (mid/endo) and TomTec-Arena feature tracking; r >= 0.7 for all; AFI-LA systematically underestimated LAS vs GE-endo and TomTec, smallest bias vs GE-mid; AFI-LA inter/intra-observer r > 0.85.

papers.title: Normal ranges of right atrial strain by contemporary echocardiography software: a prospective comparative cohort study.
papers.key_result: 100 healthy subjects (50% GE, 50% Philips scans): RA strain by TomTec 51.02 (AutoStrain LA), EchoPAC 206 (AFI-LA), VVI, Epsilon; RASr mean (LLN) 41.2% (29.6) TomTec vs 35.9% (27.0) EchoPAC; EchoPAC worked only on GE scans.

papers.title: Reference Ranges of Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain by Contemporary Vendor-Neutral Echocardiography Software in Healthy Subjects.
papers.key_result: 100 healthy subjects: LVGLS mean (LLN) -17.1% (-14.7%) TomTec 51.02 AutoStrain LV vs -17.8% (-14.4%) EchoPAC 206 AFI-LV; EchoPAC vs TomTec beta -0.62 (-1.2, 0.0); feasible on both GE and Philips scans.

papers.title: Reliability of left ventricular global longitudinal strain across acquisition and analysis techniques: a prospective comparative study.
papers.journal: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract
papers.key_result: 254 patients: 2D GLS consistent between EchoPac and TomTec-Arena (ICC > 0.9 intra/interobserver); 3D GLS lower than 2D by 4.3% (mean difference).

papers.title: Impact of inter-vendor variability on evaluation of left ventricular mechanical dispersion.
papers.key_result: 59 subjects scanned on GE and Philips: LV mechanical dispersion by EchoPac, QLAB and TomTec Arena; bias between vendor-specific packages 17.6 ms (LOA -29.6 to 64.8, r 0.47); TomTec Arena across scanner vendors bias -3.1 ms (LOA -27.6 to 21.4, r 0.75).

papers.title: Inter-vendor comparison of left atrial strain using layer specific strain analysis.
papers.key_result: 128 individuals (88 no cardiac history, 40 PAF): GE EchoPAC mid-myocardial LAS systematically lower than TomTec-Arena v2.30.02 (reservoir MD -6.08%, LOA -12% to 0%); GE endocardial LAS no systematic bias (MD 0.41%, LOA -7% to 8%).

papers.title: Three-dimensional Versus Two-Dimensional Echocardiographic Assessment of Left Atrial Volume and Deformation in Children.
papers.key_result: 50 children: 3DE LA volume/strain by GE EchoPAC 4D Auto LAQ v206 (near fully automated) vs 2DE TomTec TTA2.51 CPA (manual); processing 0.6 vs 2.7 min; good agreement for LA volume, weak agreement for LA strain.

open_questions: K213544 reports no accuracy metrics for the CNN semi-automated measurements (only that verification passed); test-set patient count, sites, vendors and demographics are not stated, and training/test independence is by random split of one pool rather than separate sites.
K201632 reports no performance data for the ML contour generation in 4D RV-Function and 4D MV-Assessment; it relies on equivalence to QLAB (K200974/K191647).
Product code discrepancy for K201632: FDA letter and openFDA list LLZ, while the 510(k) summary body lists QIH.
Predicate K150122 (TomTec-Arena TTA2, 2015) and earlier TomTec clearances are not covered in this batch.
The Knackstedt 2015 and Muraru 2016 validations concern earlier module versions (TomTec-Arena 1.2 AutoLV; earlier 4D RV-Function), not the TTA2.40/2.50 releases cleared here.

NCT07496424 ('Manual- VS Auto-Strain'; sponsor-investigator Bruno Mora, Medical University of Vienna; recruiting) evaluates fully automated intraoperative TEE strain but the record names no software vendor; it was removed from clinical_trials because its link to TOMTEC AutoStrain is unsupported.
No peer-reviewed validation of the TTA2.50 CNN semi-automated measurement feature was found in PubMed searches this session.
